messages:
morgan lee: Heads-up — found a coverage + export problem in Console audit viewer. When I filter actor_type:service_principal and export CSV some rows show truncated kms_key_id and actor fields (e.g. 'arn:aws:kms:us-1:123:...TRUNC'). Also a bunch of events from key rotation look missing from the UI (they exist in raw ES index). Anyone seen this?

raj patel: saw one report yesterday, thanks for flagging. quick q: are you seeing missing events only in the viewer or also in JSON export?

morgan lee: viewer + CSV. JSON export seems to include the full event when I hit the API directly (export?format=json) but the Console UI export pipeline appears to run a transform that compresses certain fields. Repro steps: 1) filter by actor_type:service_principal 2) open results page 3) click Export -> CSV 4) inspect kms_key_id column. Example CSV row: ```"event_time","actor_display","actor_type","kms_key_id"\n"2026-03-15T18:02:11Z","service-account-deploy","service_principal","arn:aws:kms:us-1:123456789:key/abcd1234...TRUNC"```

emma choi: that sounds bad. Product question: are customers expecting CSV to contain full KMS arns? We need to align on policy — some fields are PII-ish for certain customers.

morgan lee: it's not PII, it's a resource identifier. We redacted it earlier when we changed the UI to avoid huge columns breaking the layout, but we didn't apply the same truncation to JSON export — inconsistency. Also noticed that service-principal-rekey events are missing from viewer results (ES has docs but viewer filter by event_type:rotation doesn't surface them).

kenji watanabe: probably two issues: 1) UI transform that truncates for display is being run before export, and 2) server-side query used by viewer omits some event types because of the new schema migration (we renamed rotation->key_rotation in v2). We shipped the migration but forgot to add aliasing in the viewer query.

raj patel: confirm on namespacing — audit schema v2 added fields: "signed_event" and "kms_key_id_full" (we left legacy "kms_key_id" for backwards compat but the viewer reads legacy only). Export pipeline reads the full doc but the UI uses the legacy flattened model and a truncation helper. Fix plan: (a) add aliasing in viewer/query layer for key_rotation and rotation, (b) stop running truncation on export button, (c) add an explicit toggle: export as CSV (pretty/truncated) vs JSON (raw).

emma choi: product + legal: we should add an opt-in for full identifiers in CSV for enterprise customers with accepted TOU. Also need to show a warning modal when exporting full resource IDs (:warning:).

morgan lee: another wrinkle: service principals that assume roles generate session principals like arn:aws:sts::123:assumed-role/..., which the viewer currently normalizes to "service-account". We should preserve original arn in raw_event.actor. Proposal: store actor.raw_display in audit doc and only show redacted/normalized display in UI unless user has export:audits permission.

kenji watanabe: agree. Implementation notes: authz change required — add permission "audits.export_full" (scoped) to RBAC. Backend: export service will check token scopes and include raw fields accordingly. UI: show checkbox "Include raw identifiers (requires permission)" disabled if user lacks scope. Migration: backfill actor.raw_display for last 90 days from ES snapshot.

raj patel: security review: KMS integration question — do we need to re-encrypt stored raw identifiers under customer-managed KMS for Private customers? For hosted customers we can keep as is, but for Private/VPC must honor KMS policies.

emma choi: product: for Private we should honor customer KMS; for Hosted we'll have a configurable masking policy. Need to surface in Console settings: Audit export retention + masking.

raj patel: also add schema version field to exported JSON: audit_schema_version = "v2.1" so downstream parsers can handle aliasing. And include a small manifest file in zips that documents which fields were redacted/truncated and why.

morgan lee: deploy-bot FYI I tried to patch the viewer locally and hit a 403 when requesting export via the UI despite being org-admin. Seems the RBAC check is pointing at "audits:export" but the token is only org_admin.

deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded: audit-service v2.1.3 -> prod (2026-03-15T18:15:00Z) :rocket:

kenji watanabe: that's expected — org_admin isn't mapped to the new audits:export permission yet. I'll create a migration script to map org_admin -> audits.export for existing orgs (unless security wants stricter).

raj patel: security policy: don't auto-grant export of raw identifiers to org_admin by default. Add a tenant-level flag "allow_raw_audit_export" that must be enabled by an owner. Migration should set it to false for all tenants and create a flagged support flow for customers that request it.

emma choi: agree. Product will add the UI for owners to opt-in and legal will prepare a short consent text.

morgan lee: action items I can take: 1) PR to stop truncating on export and add checkbox, 2) backfill actor.raw_display script (dry-run first), 3) update repro steps for QA. Assigning me for 1+2.

raj patel: I'll own RBAC permission design + tenant flag + security review.

kenji watanabe: I'll handle viewer query aliasing + migration script scaffold.

emma choi: I'll own product copy + consent modal and coordinate legal.

morgan lee: cool. Leaving a link to my draft PR and sample CSV: https://git.internal/redwood/audit-ui/pull/432

kenji watanabe: noted. Let's sync tomorrow 9:30 to walk through migration plan. :calendar:

raj patel: thanks all. I'll start a short design doc for the RBAC change and tenant opt-in flow and post here when done.

morgan lee: thanks :thumbsup:
